correctness.rationale: The exact C5 square K2 graph has ten vertices, fifteen edges, and ordinary matching complex M(G), distinct from the perfect-matching subcomplex. Independently enumerated every edge subset, agreeing on all 341 nonempty faces, f-vector (15,75,145,95,11), 165 toggle pairs, one critical vertex, five 2-cells and five 3-cells; all 1020 Hasse arrows are acyclic. Independently recomputed signed integral 5x5 Morse differential matches RESULT.md entry by entry; rational rank3 and minor rows (0,1,3), columns (0,1,2) determinant -1 imply three unit Smith factors. With 2-skeleton wedge of five S2 and pi2=Z5, cancelling three primitive 3-cell attachments leaves two S2 and two S3; ordinary finite-field boundary calculations are corroborative, not the integral proof. Claim is the single n=5 prism only, no other ladder widths.

value.rationale: Agarwal and Basak (2026), arxiv:2608.30601v2, Problem 26 explicitly ask for matching-complex homotopy types of circular ladders alongside their solved perfect matching and independence complexes. C5 square K2 is the first nontrivial odd-width prism; its ordinary matching complex has a mixed S2/S3 integral homotopy wedge unlike the known contractible perfect matching subcomplex. This exact small natural instance is a meaningful witness within an explicit open research direction even without an all-n theorem.
